hypothesis_text: When the basis term structure exhibits significant steepening (8h vs 24h z-score dislocation exceeding 1.5 sigma), spot prices experience mean reversion leading to negative forward excess returns over 30m to 1h horizons across liquid perpetuals.
narrative: The perpetual-spot basis reflects market leverage, carrying cost, and immediate liquidity premia. A steepening term structure—captured by basis_term_structure_slope = safe_div(zscore(basis, '8h') - zscore(basis, '24h'), abs(zscore(basis, '24h')) + 1e-6) exceeding 1.5—identifies transient structural dislocations where short-horizon basis spikes sharply relative to medium-term basis. In liquid markets (BTC, ETH, SOL), rapid basis expansion is typically driven by aggressive leveraged positioning and taker flow rather than persistent fundamental yield shifts. As arbitrageurs step in and funding pressure mounts, basis mean-reverts, creating downward pressure on spot and perpetual prices over 30m to 1h horizons. Combining basis slope with order flow (taker_buy_ratio_1h) and book liquidity (depth_imbalance_10, spread_bps) conditions isolates moments where aggressive taker buying coincides with thin counter-liquidity, amplifying post-exhaustion reversal.
